newsitem.title: USA: Official says more tobacco talks set for next week.
newsitem.headline: Official says more tobacco talks set for next week.

text.p: Secret talks between cigarette makers and anti-smoking forces aimed at a possible settlement of lawsuits against the tobacco industry will probably resume late next week, a participant said Friday.
Arizona Attorney General Grant Woods told reporters the discussions would most likely resume next Thursday, but said he did not know where.
"We're staying in close touch with the president and members of Congress," he said. "I can't imagine doing anything they don't agree with."
Published reports have said the talks could result in the industry paying as much as $300 billion over 25 years into a compensation fund for smokers with lung cancer and other diseases.
In return, cigarette makers would get broad protection from lawsuits and would likely see higher stock market valuations on their tobacco and non-smoking businesses.
Woods said children's and public health issues rather than money were the current focus of the talks. He made the comments prior to a speech to the Ohio Association of Trial Lawyers.

Woods also said Friday's federal court ruling in North Carolina that the Food and Drug Administration has authority to regulate sales and labeling of cigarettes -- but not their advertising -- was a "remarkable victory" given that it came from a tobacco-growing region.
He said it shows the industry is "clearly going to have to make further concessions."
